topIssues.title: [L2CM]Add setWithdrawalRoute to FeeVaults
topIssues.author: maurelian
topIssues.body:
FeeVault stores recipient and withdrawalNetwork as separate fields and the proxy admin owner must update them with separate calls. withdraw is permissionless and always withdraws the full vault balance to whatever pair is stored at that moment.

This creates an unsafe intermediate state when an operator changes a vault from an L1 recipient to an L2 recipient or the reverse. If the owner updates withdrawalNetwork first, anyone can call withdraw before recipient is updated and send the full balance to the old recipient address on the new network. If the owner updates recipient first, anyone can create a withdrawal to the new recipient address on the old network.

Both the old and new configurations can be valid. The problem is the transient cross-product created by independent setters. This matters for contract recipients such as Safes, treasuries or network-specific payout contracts because the same 20-byte address may not be controlled on the other network. A public caller can therefore turn a routine route migration into a full-balance transfer or L1 withdrawal message to an address that the intended recipient cannot recover from.

topIssues.title: ci(kona-sp1): build SP1 guest ELFs in CI
topIssues.author: Inphi
topIssues.body:
### Summary

The monorepo CircleCI does **not** build the kona-sp1 guest ELFs and does not run the SP1 toolchain. Today the SP1 host-side crates build against an **empty placeholder ELF** (`rust/kona/sp1/crates/elfs/build.rs` writes a zero-byte file when no real ELF is present), so nothing in CI ever exercises the actual guest program. We need a CI job that performs the ELF build. The goal isn't to provide reproducible prestates, but to ensure that the guest program build works at all.

There are two approaches to do this:
- introduce a new docker image that handles building sp1 programs. While the upstream [sp1 docker image](https://github.com/succinctlabs/sp1/pkgs/container/sp1) exists for this purpose, it's quite phat at 1 GB. All we need is a slim environment with the sp1 toolchain installed solely to build sp1 programs.
- Install sp1 toolchain at build time

topIssues.title: op-reth: deposit contract-creation receipt `contractAddress` uses tx nonce (0) instead of deposit nonce
topIssues.author: asdv23
topIssues.body:
## Summary

For a deposit **contract-creation** transaction (`to == null`, `isCreation == true`), `eth_getTransactionReceipt` returns the wrong `contractAddress` whenever the deposit sender's L2 nonce is greater than 0.

## Component

`rust/op-reth/crates/rpc/src/eth/receipt.rs` (`OpReceiptBuilder`), via the generic `reth_rpc_eth_types::build_receipt`.

## Root cause

`build_receipt` derives the address as `from.create(tx.nonce())`. A deposit transaction's `nonce()` is hard-coded to `0` (op-alloy `TxDeposit::nonce()`), and the OP receipt builder does not override it. So the receipt reports `CREATE(from, 0)`, while the contract is actually deployed at `CREATE(from, depositNonce)` — the sender's real L2 nonce, captured during execution and stored on the receipt as `depositNonce`.

The `depositNonce` lives only as a **receipt field** (set during execution); it is never written back into the transaction's `nonce`, so the RPC derivation has no way to recover it without an explicit override.

## Expected (op-geth parity)

op-geth derives the deposit creation address from the deposit nonce, in both construction and `DeriveFields` (go-ethereum `core/types/receipt.go`):

```go
nonce := context.Tx.Nonce()
if context.Tx.IsDepositTx() && r.DepositNonce != nil {
    nonce = *r.DepositNonce
}
r.ContractAddress = crypto.CreateAddress(from, nonce)
```

## Reproduction (observed)

Same deposit contract-creation tx, two clients on the same chain:

| client  | `contractAddress`             | `depositNonce` |
|---------|-------------------------------|----------------|
| op-reth | `CREATE(from, 0)` (wrong)     | 35964          |
| op-geth | `CREATE(from, 35964)` (correct) | 35964        |

`eth_getCode(receipt.contractAddress)` returns the deployed runtime code only at the op-geth address; op-reth's address returns `0x`.

## Impact

- RPC-derived field only — no consensus, state-root, or persistence impact; the contract is correctly deployed.
- Only affects deposit + `isCreation` + sender L2 nonce > 0 (rare path), which is why it has gone unnoticed.

## Fix

PR #21449 overrides `contract_address` in `OpReceiptBuilder` using the deposit nonce already present on the receipt, mirroring op-geth.

topPRs.title: feat(kona): add kona-sp1 range-executor + SP1 execute action test
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
Add an SP1 execute test harness so the `kona-sp1` range guest can be exercised end-to-end by op-e2e action tests, mirroring the native fault-proof program harness.

- New `kona-sp1-range-executor` binary: takes the native kona-host `single` boot inputs, generates the witness via the kona-host preimage server, runs the range guest in SP1 execute mode (no proving), reads the committed `BootInfoStruct`, and exits 0 (valid) / 1 (invalid claim) / 2 (infra), matching the native fault-proof exit-code convention.
- Go wiring: `rustbin.RunKonaSP1Range` (shared oracle-server exec path), `RunRangeExecutor` + `ProgramRunner` refactor in the proofs helpers, `RunSP1RangeProgram` env method, and `TestSP1RangeSimpleEmptyChain`.
- just recipes (`build-range-executor`, `action-tests-sp1`) + README section.

The test skips unless `KONA_SP1_RANGE_EXECUTOR_PATH` is set and is not yet wired into a CI job (needs the Dockerized SP1 ELF build in CircleCI). It covers the honest-claim path only; the host-side witness generator rejects invalid claims before the guest runs, so invalid-claim coverage is a follow-up.

topPRs.title: fix(op-batcher): prevent panic when a pruned channel's tx confirms late
topPRs.author: damilolaedwards
topPRs.body:
Channel pruning was decoupled from tx confirmation, so a late tx
confirmation could resolve to a channel whose blocks were already pruned,
making rewindToBlock compute an out-of-range (unsigned-underflowed) index
and panic. Two cases are handled:

- PruneChannels now removes the pruned channels' entries from txChannels,
  so a late confirmation of a fully-pruned channel is ignored rather than
  resolving to a removed channel.
- rewindToBlock no longer indexes out of range when its target block has
  already become safe and been pruned (e.g. a channel straddling the safe
  head whose leading block was dropped by PruneSafeBlocks): it returns when
  there is nothing pending and clamps to the oldest pending block instead
  of underflowing, while still panicking on a genuinely-absent block.

topPRs.title: refactor(kona): make sp1 range core natively testable
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
Refactors the kona-sp1 range program so most of its logic can be exercised natively without paying the SP1 execute cost for every coverage case. Otherwise, it takes approx 30 seconds on my machine to run a simple action test with the sp1 (riscv emulated) executor. 

The SP1 guest remains the ELF/stdin/public-values boundary, while the derivation and execution core is shared with native tests and a new fast executor mode.
